title: Karna
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a colleague of Shmuel, as in Shabbat 108. Shmuel and Karna were sitting on the bank of the Nehar Malka River — Shmuel said to him, 'A great man is coming from the West and has a stomach ailment — go, test his learning.' He went and found Rav, and Karna asked him several questions and vexed him. He said to him, 'What is your name?' He said, 'Karna.' He said to him, 'May it be His will that a horn (karna) come out of your eye.' And in Bava Batra 89 it appears that he was punished through Shmuel, and Rashbam explained that this and that were both the cause.
And in Kiddushin 44b there is a dispute between Shmuel and Karna.

Hyman reports that in the Yerushalmi, Bava Batra, at the supplied locator צ״ה, halakhah 5, when the Exilarch seized Rav and imprisoned him, Karna (spelled גרנא here) came in and set him free, and there he is called by the name Rav Karna.
And in Sanhedrin 17b they said 'the judges of the Exile: Karna,' which Hyman explains as meaning that he and Shmuel were judges in Nehardea.

And Hyman writes that he composed baraitot, as in Bava Kamma 47b: 'Rav Yehuda bar Simon taught in the Nezikin of the school of Karna,' and in Sanhedrin 30a: 'Rav Idi bar Avin taught in the Nezikin of the school of Karna.' (And H-R-Ch and the Arukh explained that in tractate Nezikin, an external Mishnah, Karna was the one who taught it.)
And likewise we find in Bava Kamma 4a that Karna taught: 'four primary categories of damages, and man is one of them.'
And in Bava Kamma, chapter 8, halakha 6: 'Rav Karna taught: for a kick, one.' And there in chapter 9, halakha 2: 'Rav Karna taught: even if he stole a calf, etc.'
He is mentioned in Ketubot 111a and Kiddushin 44a [supplied; consulted saying at 44b]: 'Karna said: there is something behind this.'

notes.text: Shabbat108a in the named Davidson text has Shmuel ask Karna to test Rav’s learning; the subsequent questions explain the idiom. There is something behind this is an idiom, not words are within.

The supplied Yerushalmi locator צ״ה and spelling גרנא still require a matching witness. Hyman’s Nezikin of the school of Karna is a baraita/external-Mishnah collection, not an independent claim about canonical Mishnah authorship.

The supplied dashes in the opening Shabbat narrative are retained. Two whole saved William Davidson Shabbat108a Hebrew paragraphs support Shmuel sending Karna to test Rav's learning and the name/horn exchange; they are two paragraphs of one digital witness, not independent sources or a whole-folio collation. The additional legal answers and verses in the longer paragraph are not imported. Hyman's colleague claim, joint judges in Nehardea, baraita authorship and commentary reports remain his assertions. H-R-Ch preserves the supplied הר״ח abbreviation here; the earlier Rabbenu Chananel expansion remains archived without a fresh commentary collation. The external Mishnah/Nezikin collection claim does not establish canonical Mishnah authorship. The Yerushalmi locator צ״ה, halakhah5, the supplied גרנא spelling and prison narrative retain their source hold. The earlier test-his-learning and something-behind-this idioms remain; Bava Batra/Rashbam and other listed citations were not freshly read as whole named passages in this review. All original and current mixed notes remain preserved, including their earlier printed-wording claims, without fresh printing-history proof.

The whole Shabbat 108a paragraphs support Shmuel sending Karna to test Rav and Rav’s name-and-horn reply. Bava Batra 89a gives the separate Shmuel episode: he instructs Karna to teach oversight of measures but not prices; Karna teaches both, and the horn follows. The whole Rashbam gloss explicitly says that both events caused it, supporting Hyman’s reconciliation. The whole consulted Yerushalmi Bava Batra 5:5 has Rav Karna visit the imprisoned Rav, followed by Rav telling him to go out and speak; it does not explicitly say that Karna secured Rav’s release. Hyman’s supplied צ״ה, גרנא and release summary remain visible as his account. Sanhedrin 17b names Karna as “judges of the Exile”; the joint Nehardea court with Shmuel remains Hyman’s explanation, not a universal identity rule. The Nezikin-school reports are directly present in Bava Kamma 47b and Sanhedrin 30b, beside Hyman’s 30a; they do not independently establish sole authorship or canonical Mishnah editorship. The whole Bava Kamma 4a paragraph names Karna’s four categories; Yerushalmi Bava Kamma 8:6 reads Rav Qarni beside the supplied Karna, and 9:2 names Rav Karna in the calf passage. Kiddushin 44b has the Shmuel–Karna dispute and דברים בגו, beside the final supplied 44a. Exact H-R-Ch and Arukh editions remain uncollated; none of these variant names is globally merged. In the 8:6 list, “for a kick, one” gives an amount, rather than saying “for one kick”; no unspecified denomination is inserted into Hyman’s words.
